correctness.rationale: The proof checks every possible factor location in the two-copy Cantor recursion. Non-letter binary Lyndon factors begin in 0 and end in 1. A factor spanning the new middle zero-run cannot begin in the old left copy because its middle run is longer than its initial run. If it begins in the middle run, the initial exponent exceeds the old maximum exactly when it creates a new Lyndon factor; for the remaining exponents, the candidate is either already present in the old copy or fails the proper-suffix test by the old middle gap. Distinct factor counts follow by counting the initial exponent and right-hand prefixes ending in 1. Complete independently enumerated factor sets agree at ranks 0 through 5, but finite tests are not the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact all-ranks factor-language classification has a natural invariant: distinct Lyndon factors of canonical finite Cantor substitution iterates. It identifies precisely how the new central zero-run creates genuinely new Lyndon strings, implies a lengthwise spectrum recursion, and gives a nontrivial growth exponent log_3(6) relative to word length. This is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a generic textbook deduction of the exact number.
